claims.statement: create_app builds the FastAPI app and publishes the shared collaborators on app.state — settings, store, model_cache (factory) plus worker and proxy (lifespan) — so the routers stay stateless and resolve everything through request.app.state.

When OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_EXTRA_HEADERS is configured, create_app parses it during construction so malformed JSON aborts startup instead of failing the first request; routers register health then wikis and a root GET / returns {service, docs, health, wikis} with include_in_schema=False.

Lifespan startup purges expired terminal wikis with purge_expired(job_retention_hours) and requeues claims whose heartbeat is older than worker_lease_seconds with recover_stale, then launches the asyncio task openwiki-reaper running _reap_loop, which repeats recover_stale plus prune_workers every worker_reap_seconds and suppresses all exceptions so reaping never stops.

Only when RUN_LOCAL_WORKER is true does the lifespan start an in-process WorkerLoop (the same loop used by python -m app.worker) and publish app.state.worker / app.state.proxy; shutdown cancels the reaper and stops the worker, and app.state.proxy stays None otherwise.

POST /wikis validates source.url through ingestion.validate_git_url with allow_local taken from settings.allow_local_git, translating any IngestionError into HTTP 422; unsupported schemes such as ftp, empty URLs, and local paths or file:// while ALLOW_LOCAL_GIT is false are all rejected before the job is created.

POST /wikis rejects auth.token unless the validated URL starts with http:// or https://, answering 422 with "auth.token is only supported for http(s) git URLs", so tokens are never used for SSH or local sources.

When push is enabled, POST /wikis enforces three additional preconditions with 422: scp-like git@ or ssh:// URLs (no SSH keys in the service), git:// URLs, and http(s) URLs without source.auth.token; an invalid push.branch or empty push.message is rejected earlier as a schema validation error.

POST /wikis persists a source dict of {"type": "git", "url", "ref", "token"} together with language, concurrency, mode and an optional push.model_dump(), then returns 202 with _accepted(wiki_id): a WikiAccepted whose status is always queued and whose links are {status: /wikis/{id}, logs: /wikis/{id}/logs, download: /wikis/{id}/download}.

POST /wikis/upload normalizes the client filename with Path(...).name, requires a suffix among ingestion.SUPPORTED_ARCHIVE_SUFFIXES (422 otherwise listing them), creates the job row before streaming the body into jobs/<wiki_id>/upload<suffix>, and enforces MAX_UPLOAD_MB while streaming; exceeding the limit deletes the partial file and the just-created job and answers 413, so no orphan queued job survives a rejected upload.

POST /wikis/{id}/cancel maps store outcomes: a queued wiki is cancelled immediately with error "cancelled before start", a running wiki only sets cancel_requested=1 and returns "cancelling" (cooperative cancellation detected at the next heartbeat), a terminal wiki yields 409, and an unknown id yields 404.

POST /wikis/{id}/retry re-enqueues only failed or cancelled wikis — clearing error, progress, finished_at and the whole claim so OpenWiki resumes from its own openwiki/.run.json — and answers 202 WikiAccepted; not_retryable becomes 409 with the current status in the detail and an unknown id becomes 404.
GET /wikis lists wikis newest-first as list[WikiView] with limit constrained to 1..500 and defaulting to 50, backed by the store's ORDER BY created_at DESC query.

GET /wikis/{id}/logs requires the wiki to exist (404 otherwise), returns an empty body when the log file does not exist yet, and tails the file with collections.deque(maxlen=tail) where tail is constrained to 1..MAX_LOG_TAIL (2000) and defaults to 50.

GET /wikis/{id}/download distinguishes an unknown wiki (404 "wiki not found") from a known wiki whose wiki.zip is missing (404 "wiki is not ready (status=...)", which is the case while a generation is still running or after a failure before packaging), and serves the artifact as application/zip with filename openwiki-{wiki_id}.zip.

DELETE /wikis/{id} returns 409 with "wiki is still running" unless the status is terminal (done/failed/cancelled), and on success removes both the SQLite row and the whole jobs/<wiki_id>/ directory before answering 204.

GET /health is deliberately cheap and never calls a model: it reports status ok, the app version, openwiki_bin plus openwiki_found (resolved by splitting the configured command and calling shutil.which on its first argv token), data_dir, pool = store.stats() counting recently seen workers, and the passive model configuration snapshot from describe_model.

GET /health/model runs the active probe through app.state.model_cache.check(force=...) and maps the probe status to HTTP: ok and unsupported return 200 while not_configured and error return 503; the JSON body always carries status and detail, and provider errors and endpoints are redacted so credentials cannot leak.

ModelStatusCache serializes probes per app instance behind an asyncio.Lock and reuses a result for MODEL_CHECK_TTL_SECONDS, returning it with cached=true; force=true bypasses a fresh cache entry and re-probes, so concurrent /health/model calls trigger a single upstream request.

The request/response contracts live in app/schemas.py: WikiStatus enumerates queued/fetching/generating/finalizing/done/failed/cancelled; WikiCreate requires source: GitSource and constrains language to 2..32 chars, concurrency to 1..8 and mode to the literal auto|init|update; PushOptions validates the target branch name and a non-empty commit message; PushResult.status is one of pushed/no_changes/failed/skipped. The /wikis/upload form fields reuse only part of that contract: concurrency is constrained to 1..8 and mode to the same literal, but the language form field is a plain optional string with no length constraint.

wiki_to_view is the single mapping from the internal job record to the public WikiView: it redacts git URLs and drops the stored token, renames claimed_by to worker, coerces attempts to int, re-validates the push/push_result JSON columns into PushOptions/PushResult only when they are dicts, and exposes filename with an empty source_url for upload sources.

Because the API only enqueues and the store is the coordination point, domain failures never surface as 5xx: routers translate typed store outcomes and IngestionError into 422/404/409/413, and the wiki status lifecycle (queued → fetching → generating → finalizing → done, plus failed/cancelled and requeue-on-stale) is produced entirely by claim_next, heartbeat and complete.

Settings in app/core/config.py directly change API behavior: MAX_UPLOAD_MB bounds the upload stream (413 threshold), JOB_RETENTION_HOURS controls startup purge of terminal wikis (0 keeps them forever), WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS and WORKER_REAP_SECONDS control stale-claim requeue, RUN_LOCAL_WORKER decides whether a worker runs in-process, ALLOW_LOCAL_GIT enables local/file:// sources on POST /wikis, and MODEL_CHECK_TTL_SECONDS/MODEL_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS shape GET /health/model.

The service is designed with no authentication on the API — it is intended for an internal network or behind an authenticated reverse proxy — and the container healthcheck probes /health every 15s, so /health must stay fast and model-free.

The HTTP surface is covered end to end by tests using fastapi.testclient.TestClient with the fake OpenWiki CLI and RUN_LOCAL_WORKER=true: tests/test_api_wikis.py exercises 422/202/404/409 outcomes, polling to terminal states, restart persistence and crash resume; tests/test_health.py asserts /health returns pool.workers == 1 and / points at /docs; tests/test_push.py covers the router-level push validations and the push_result contract.

Every {wiki_id} path parameter is resolved through JobStore.get, which rejects ids not matching the 32-hex JOB_ID_RE pattern, so an unknown or malformed id (e.g. deadbeef or ..%2Fescape) yields the same 404 "wiki not found" without ever touching a filesystem path built from the id.

tests/test_provider_proxy.py covers the factory fail-fast on malformed OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_EXTRA_HEADERS and the loopback proxy wiring: with an in-process worker plus extra headers and a base URL configured, create_app exposes a non-None app.state.proxy whose base_url addresses 127.0.0.1, and OpenWiki receives that loopback URL as OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL.
